For every follow-up request to "continue" an ongoing development, audit, or CI/PR cleanup initiative, **begin the user-visible response with a concise state report before changing code or PRs**:

## Navigation visual stability specialization (Mobile Web / Web / PWA / Desktop)

**Permanent no-jitter contract / P78 — MANDATORY for every future UI PR.** Read [docs/mobile-navigation-stability.md](docs/mobile-navigation-stability.md) BEFORE changing Files, Gallery, album folders, Viewer, Source, Search/Trash, Sidebar, settings, app navigation, deep links, pagination, or asynchronous loading. A correct-looking final screenshot is NOT acceptance. These rules apply to new pages, refactors and all four clients; page jitter is a blocking regression, not optional polish.

1. **ONE authorized visual commit per navigation.** A click, route update, Promise resolution, cache hit, loading=false or 300ms timer is only intent, NOT authorization to reveal the destination. For another folder/album/collection, retain last accepted rows/crumbs/rail, stable scroll-host DOM identity, scrollTop, saved folder ID and Viewer return anchor until current Owner/session/lifecycle/request generation AND canonical authorized first counted Range or index receipt match the target. Reveal the new view and update scroll/storage ONCE in the pre-paint commit. FORBID beginBrowse/scrollTo(0)/virtualizer reset/clearing old rows or writing target storage in asynchronous acknowledgement callbacks before that receipt. Failed, canceled, stale, denied or superseded requests must leave the previous committed presentation unchanged. Same-folder activation may skip a redundant read only when that exact accepted destination is already verified.
2. **Never create an ephemeral intermediate UI.** FORBID ordinary folder/album/app/rail navigation screens, captions or spinner/skeleton rows such as “正在加载文件夹…”, “正在读取相册…”, or an inserted progress ring after a 300ms delay, even for genuinely slow GETs. Suppress only the decorative display, NEVER the real network request. A cold/unverified screen reserves a persistent silent slot, exposes truthful aria-busy, and must not show an invented error or zero. No blank→error→loading→content, accepted rows→spinner→rows, moving breadcrumb/header, or extra scroll host. Retry, actual terminal error and accepted data remain visible.
3. **Verified data, not Boolean busy, owns empty/error.** Track unverified / ready / error for current Owner + source + query/directory + generation. Initial empty array/null or loading=false BEFORE useEffect runs does NOT prove “暂无/空文件夹/还没有相册” or request failure. Only an accepted, current, authenticated ready-zero may display empty. Keep last verified rows or verified-empty on same-owner refresh; distinguish terminal first-request failure from unrequested state, preserve actionable retry, and never paint another Owner's cached data. Fence every late callback and cancellation.
4. **Geometry and scroll must be stable.** Preserve xDrive 52px global app header, one mounted Files/Gallery virtual scroll host, and existing Viewer anchor/focus. Cold, pending, accepted-empty and error states on the same surface MUST use identical reserved minimum geometry. Toolbar, Search, Sidebar, crumbs, pagination and loading indicators may not conditionally insert/remove rows or change height. FORBID height/maxHeight/padding/margin/top/list-layout animation in response to scrolling or short busy flags; keep 44px touch targets, keyboard focus and reduced-motion behavior. Do not add a second virtualizer, materialize 100k entries, or schedule another scroll-to-top effect.
5. **Explicit real-progress exceptions, NOT a spinner loophole.** Preserve real asynchronous thumbnail/file preview, Live Photo resource, video poster, upload/download/sync progress, user-invoked indexing, durable operations, Search/Trash, and legitimate page/viewport fetch feedback when genuinely useful. If shown, feedback must use a reserved non-reflowing slot and truthful state rather than a decorative navigation timer. Never disable AbortController, Go ctx cancellation, retry or error disclosure to mask a spinner. Do not blanket-disable all CSS transitions or accessibility cues.
6. **Mandatory tests and evidence on EVERY affected entry.** Update tests mounting the ORIGINAL React components plus a built Chromium browser navigation scenario (or explicitly justify an unavailable platform/entry). Force before-first-GET loading=false, fast and held >300ms response, accepted zero/nonzero, terminal failure/retry, out-of-order and rapidly superseded requests, owner switch, back/deep link, Viewer return, scroll. Assert ONE scroll host, same old visible anchor/title/saved ID during pending, exactly ONE reset only after success; verify header/crumb/scroll-host rectangles within 1 CSS px during held navigation. Never assert that an overscanned first DOM row is the user's visible anchor. Test Web wide, Mobile Web 375/390/899px, Desktop and installed PWA; report native iOS Safari/Android/orientation/keyboard/slow WAN as NOT RUN until physically checked. Continue the existing P58-P77 mounted/browser suites; extend new surfaces instead of only adding another static string test. See [desktop/tests/navigation-no-jitter-contract-p78.cjs](desktop/tests/navigation-no-jitter-contract-p78.cjs).
7. **Mandatory PR / release gate.** Every navigation, loading/readState, spinner/skeleton, route, geometry, scroll or Range change MUST document previous committed content, authenticated receipt boundary, before/held/after frames, failure/retry, and cross-platform effect. A newly appearing intermediate frame or unexplained layout movement BLOCKS merge. Require exact-HEAD full CI, actual relevant renderer + Chromium regression and Final Gate; distinguish source-tested, built-browser-tested, physically measured and merged. Do NOT invent CLS/FPS, claim iOS physical parity or mark release GO from desktop Chromium emulation. Keep independent Go Race, security, transfers and physical 100k performance benchmarks separately scoped.

**Permanent visual-generation fence / P88 — mandatory.** Every delayed visual status must be bound to the exact current request/scope/pending cycle. A plain Boolean spinner visibility or scope-only delayed status from the previous request MUST NOT be reused: clearing it in useEffect runs AFTER paint and can show one wrong frame. Increment an in-render monotonically increasing presentation generation whenever pending changes, the scope changes, or the feedback delay changes; compare the stored timer generation BEFORE returning visible feedback. Clean up obsolete timers in the effect without delaying, canceling or swallowing real network requests. This rule applies to Web, Mobile Web, PWA and Desktop Files, Gallery, album/People/Places, Source, Task/Transfer, settings and new async pages. Ordinary navigation never receives a decorative loader (even after 300ms); preserve verified old rows, breadcrumbs, scroll owner and anchor until an authorized counted first Range/index commits, or hold an identical silent first-read slot with truthful aria-busy. Real thumbnails/posters/Live Photo, Search, populated Trash refresh, and true upload/download/sync/task progress remain independently visible in fixed geometry. Do not animate virtualizer width, height, margin, padding or list geometry; keep the 52px App Header and 44px controls. Mandatory evidence on every affected entry: fresh mount, fast/sustained >300ms, same-key repeated requests, changed key/delay, canceled/stale, verified zero/error/retry, rapid navigation and original scroll anchor; test actual mounted React and built browser 375/390/899px, wide Web/Desktop. New assertions belong in desktop/tests/navigation-feedback-generation-p88.cjs and original P78 suites. Actual native iOS/Android, installed PWA, real WAN and physical 100k/CLS/FPS remain NOT RUN until specifically measured. Violations block the PR.

## Push/Pull apps and device-local backup ownership (2026-10-10)

Read `docs/sync-folder-apps.md` and `docs/local-folder-push.md` before changing synchronization-folder UI, routes, Source handlers, device registration, or execution permissions.

- **Two first-level applications**, not two tabs or a parent navigation item: **设备备份** (Push) and **远程拉取** (Pull). Internal connector records remain **Source / 同步文件夹** for API/storage compatibility, but user-visible **远程拉取** screens must call them **拉取来源** (or simply 来源), not 同步文件夹; omit redundant Pull/Push direction badges in the Pull-only app. **设备备份** uses backup/device wording. Never rename persisted paths, Source IDs, or transports for a display-copy change. Keep the existing full-screen App Frame, 52px global title bar, unified shared MUI fundamentals, and shared Server `Source / SourceItem / SyncRun / Planner / CAS` contracts. Separate business controllers, creation flows, detail views, application routes and state; route legacy `sync-folders?source=ID` links by persisted `direction`, never by `kind` alone.
- **Push is device-local, including under the same signed-in account.** The Desktop on physical device A may create/configure/preview/start/pause/cancel/retry/remove *only sources whose locally authorized Root belongs to device A*. Desktop B may **view only** A's backups, just like Web/Mobile Web; never treat another user's login, the same account, a host name, Web origin, `User-Agent`, or caller-controlled device headers as local execution authority. An Agent's already-authorized background schedule may run without an open Desktop window. Never make closing a window a durable-sync cancel command.
- **Read-only visibility scope B:** for authorized owner devices show device name/platform, trusted heartbeat or explicitly unknown state, Source/folder display name, Server-resolved cloud target, backup policy, real progress and totals, and paginated run summaries/history. Remote/Desktop-other and Web/Mobile Web must not receive local absolute paths, Root fingerprints, device credentials, detailed local file listings, raw failure strings that reveal such paths, mutable Source contracts or operation actions. Use a deliberately redacted read DTO; do not rely on hiding an edit button.
- **Local-only mutation must be enforced by the Server and owning Agent**, before activating `local_folder`: prove possession of the bound device credential plus authorization for that exact Root and Source/revision at each mutating boundary. Owner JWT alone can authorize safe reads, not remote Source create/config/trigger/cancel/delete or binding mutation. A revoked or different device cannot execute stale work. Preserve old Source ID/Node/SourceItem/alias/history and Backups' two-complete-scans/24h/trash-only Mirror safety. Do not lift existing local Source activation/Run gates early.
- **Account-security exception:** a signed-in owner may remotely **revoke lost-device authentication** from an independent account-security control, with appropriate audit/owner scope. That action never starts/stops/changes a Push Source and is NOT a button in 设备备份. Revocation invalidates subsequent device-authorized operations; do not promise instant termination of a durable transfer without its own verified fencing/cancel contract.
- **NAS Push:** NAS remains its own local execution/configuration authority. This round builds **no new NAS agent, NAS pairing, remote operation, general-device binding or NAS Push manager**. The new 设备备份 UI reserves a clearly non-operational **待支持** NAS entry only. Preserve legacy NAS CLI-created Source records, committed bytes, histories and background operation; document any legacy owner-JWT remote-control endpoint as a transitional security gap rather than claiming enforced local-only NAS controls.
- **Pull:** Yike Photos, Synology Photos Pull and Synology File Station Pull remain Server-executed and fully manageable from Web/Desktop; preserve cookie/DSM secret contracts, schedules, scan/run/retry, current target binding, owners and existing transport. Classify `synology_photos` by **`kind + direction`**, because it exists in both families. Generic-source endpoints must reject disallowed local Push writes by device identity without breaking Pull.
- **Verification and handoff:** tests must cover A controlling A, Desktop B/Web viewing (including accurate progress and history) but failing every A write even if both Desktop installs share an account, forged headers/device IDs, revoked devices, unknown heartbeat, path/error redaction, account-security revocation only, old deep links, existing Source IDs, Pull full parity, and NAS placeholder/legacy data retention. Distinguish implemented, CI-tested, merged and physically measured states in every continuation report. Use the canonical phased checklist in `docs/sync-folder-apps.md`.

## Repository workflow

For every code change in this repository, use this workflow by default:

Provider delivery rules:

- **GitLab:** after the applicable local validation passes, make a normal commit on the latest GitLab `master` and push it directly to `gitlab/master`. Never force-push. Treat the resulting GitLab `master` pipeline as the authoritative post-push validation; if it fails, diagnose it and fix forward with another normally pushed commit.
- **GitHub:** never push changes directly to `origin/master`. Push an exactly-one-commit short-lived branch, open a PR targeting `master`, require the PR CI to pass, and merge it with linear history.
- **Changes for both providers:** start from a commit shared by both masters whenever possible, validate locally, push the commit directly to GitLab `master`, and push that same commit to a short-lived GitHub branch for a PR. Do not push it directly to GitHub `master`.

1. Run `git fetch origin` and `git fetch gitlab` first when both remotes exist.
2. Before creating or continuing a work branch, reconcile only branches that are materially related to the current task, dependency chain, or touched subsystem:
   - inspect related unmerged branches for their diff, PR/MR state, CI state, conflicts, and unfinished work;
   - continue a viable related branch instead of duplicating the same work;
   - delete related branches whose commits are already fully contained in `origin/master`, or that are abandoned, duplicate, or superseded;
   - keep a related branch only when there is a concrete reason it cannot yet be merged or deleted, and state that reason.
   Do **not** inspect, wait on, merge, rebase, or otherwise manage unrelated branches/PRs/MRs merely because they exist. Unrelated work may proceed independently unless it creates an actual merge conflict or changes a dependency required by the current task.
   Do not start a fresh implementation while an older viable half-finished branch for the same or directly related work is still unresolved.
3. After reconciling the current task's related branches, fix the work baseline immediately and do not let unrelated later `master` movement churn the branch. GitLab work may continue on a clean local `master` based on `gitlab/master`; GitHub work uses a new short-lived branch from the selected `origin/master` baseline when no related existing branch should be continued. Create or preserve the branch's single work commit immediately after selecting that baseline.
   - Every short-lived work branch must carry **exactly one work commit above its selected base at all times after the first commit is created**. Do not accumulate follow-up, fixup, or "temporary" commits with the intention of squashing them later.
   - After the first commit, fold every subsequent change into that same work commit with `git commit --amend` (and force-push only the non-`master` work branch when needed). Keep the branch single-commit throughout development, review fixes, and pre-merge reconciliation.
   - For closely related dependent phases, do **not** wait for an upstream PR/MR to merge before continuing. Pull/reuse the active work branch directly, or create a short-lived stacked branch from its current tested head when that is the fastest safe path.
   - A stacked/dependent branch must likewise add exactly one work commit above its immediate dependency branch. After the dependency lands, rebase/reconstruct that one commit onto the latest `origin/master`; never use a late squash as normal cleanup.
   - Do not block implementation merely because a related PR is waiting on CI/review when the dependency branch is available and its current tree is suitable for continued work.
4. Make the requested change only on the selected delivery branch, or on the clean local `master` selected for a GitLab direct push. Preserve the one-work-commit invariant on every short-lived GitHub branch.
5. Add or update relevant tests.
6. Run the applicable local tests and require them to pass before opening or updating the PR/MR.
7. Before the first delivery push, fetch the target remote again to detect real integration problems, but do not chase unrelated `master` movement after the work baseline has been fixed. For GitHub, keep the existing single work commit on its selected baseline when the PR remains mergeable; reconstruct that one commit onto the newer `origin/master` only when GitHub reports the PR cannot be merged because of an actual conflict, or when repository rules explicitly require an update. For GitLab, update the clean local `master` from `gitlab/master` before committing or pushing. Do not rebase merely because `master` has unrelated newer commits or merely to retrigger CI.
8. Before the first full GitHub PR validation, verify that the work branch is already exactly one commit relative to its merge base; do **not** plan a final squash after CI. For a normal branch based on `origin/master`, verify with:

   ```bash
   git rev-list --count origin/master..HEAD
   ```

   The result must be `1`. A result greater than `1` is a workflow violation to fix before full PR/MR validation, not an expected pre-merge cleanup step. The purpose of keeping the branch single-commit from the start is to avoid a late squash/force-push that causes an otherwise unnecessary additional CI run.
9. For GitHub, push the branch and open or update the PR; its CI is the authoritative pre-merge validation. For GitLab, push the locally validated commit directly to `gitlab/master`; its `master` pipeline is the authoritative post-push validation. Once the applicable pipeline is green, do not push, rebase, amend, squash, or otherwise retrigger CI unless the source tree must change.
10. If `origin/master` advances after CI is green, ignore unrelated commits and merge the already-tested PR directly when it remains mergeable. Reconstruct/rebase only when repository rules require it or an actual merge conflict makes the PR unmergeable. Any required reconstruction changes the tested commit and therefore requires the PR/MR CI to run again.
11. Merge an already-single-commit GitHub PR into `master` using a linear-history merge. GitLab changes are already on `master` through the validated normal push. Do not rely on squash merge to repair a multi-commit work branch.
   - For GitHub, the successful PR CI run is the merge gate. **After the PR merge succeeds, do not wait for, poll, or block subsequent work on the `master` push CI triggered by that merge.** Proceed immediately to cleanup and the next task.
   - Treat GitHub `master` CI as an asynchronous post-merge defense, not a second completion gate for the already-merged PR. If that later pipeline reports a regression attributable to the merged change, diagnose it and fix forward in a new normal PR; unrelated follow-on work must not wait for that pipeline to finish.
12. After the merge succeeds, delete the merged remote branch through the repository cleanup automation:
   - GitHub: `.github/workflows/cleanup-merged-branches.yml` runs on pushes to `master` and safely removes redundant merged branches, including rebase-merged PR branches whose original head SHA no longer appears in `master` history.
   - If an automatic cleanup run is missed or delayed, use that workflow's `workflow_dispatch` entry point instead of requiring a locally authenticated branch-delete command.
   - Verify the merged branch is gone after cleanup; do not leave superseded task branches around.
13. Keep long-lived branches to a minimum.

## Race and concurrency specialization policy

- **Mandatory Race registry and de-duplication:** Before any Race/concurrency investigation, read [`docs/race-test-registry.md`](docs/race-test-registry.md) and compare the exact subsystem, competing operations, forced interleaving, identity/lifecycle and platform. Do not repeat accepted unchanged scenarios merely to restart a new chat. New source changes, new orderings/platforms, regressions and mandatory exact-head CI are legitimate repeat reasons. In the same one-work-commit PR, record every new meaningful probe and its authentic test-only First-red, rejected/invalid harness failures, unchanged reproducer, repaired exact-head CI and merge/branch disposition in that registry. Never claim an unrun test, physical E2E or GitLab validation.

- For a race/concurrency specialization task, **test first and do not change production behavior until a real failure is reproduced**. Continue running or extending the relevant race/stress/interleaving tests until one of them fails because of an actual product concurrency/lifecycle bug.
- A test harness, fixture, mock, parser, selector, timing assumption, CI infrastructure issue, or unrelated existing failure does **not** count as the required reproduction. Fix the test/harness itself and rerun without changing production code.
- The first-red evidence must be deterministic enough to identify the violated contract (for example: stale completion overwrites a newer scope, old lifecycle retains busy ownership, duplicate same-tick submission, old request crosses account/session identity, or a newer revision is regressed). Record that failing assertion/path in the PR description or test name.
- If no real race failure can be reproduced, keep testing/auditing; do not land speculative synchronization, generation fences, locks, cancellation, or lifecycle resets merely because a race appears theoretically possible.
- Only after a real first-red is confirmed may production code be changed. Make the smallest fix that addresses the reproduced ordering/lifecycle failure, and preserve existing platform semantics unless the failing contract proves they are wrong.
- After the fix, require the **same reproducer** to turn green, then run the materially related race/concurrency suite and normal subsystem tests. A replacement test that avoids the original failing interleaving is not sufficient.
- Race/concurrency branches follow the normal related-work rule: inspect and continue viable related branches/PRs first, avoid duplicate fixes, and keep the GitHub branch at exactly one work commit. Test-first revisions and production fixes must be amended into that same work commit rather than accumulated as fixup commits.
- Merge only after the reproduced race is fixed, the relevant regression suite is green, and the repository's normal authoritative CI gate passes. Do not merge a branch that is only statically plausible, partially tested, or still failing the original race.
- This policy applies equally to FileExplorer, Gallery/Photo UI, transfers, thumbnails, background tasks, sync, navigation/session lifecycle, caches, and any other subsystem where the task is specifically a race/concurrency investigation.

- Before starting or continuing a performance task, inspect only the materially related open branches/PRs/MRs and the canonical performance document for that subsystem. Continue a viable related branch before opening a duplicate implementation. Already-merged, superseded, or abandoned performance branches must not be treated as active work.
- Every performance track must have a canonical document under `docs/` (for FileExplorer, use `docs/file-explorer-performance.md`). The document is part of the performance contract, not optional release notes.
- Every performance PR/MR must update its canonical performance document in the **same change** with the current status and evidence for that specific work item. Record at minimum: status, workload/data shape, scale, benchmark or trace command/tool, sample count when applicable, BEFORE baseline, AFTER/current result, units, delta, acceptance/rejection decision, regression budget when one exists, and the next action.
- Performance optimization is measurement-gated: **measure the current implementation first on the stable named workload before changing production code**. If the current result is already within the documented budget/acceptance target, keep the implementation unchanged and record that decision. If it is not, state the acceptance threshold before experimenting, make the smallest performance change, then rerun the **same workload, environment, units, and sampling method**. Keep the production change only when the improvement is material and repeatable beyond normal benchmark noise and no important CPU/RSS/I/O/request-count/correctness dimension regresses; otherwise revert the production change and record the experiment as **Rejected / no material gain** with its BEFORE/AFTER evidence.
- Use explicit status labels such as **Planned**, **Benchmarking**, **Measured baseline**, **In progress**, **Accepted**, **Rejected**, and **Merged**. Do not leave a completed optimization documented as merely planned, and do not leave an active benchmark without a status.
- If a change has no comparable wall-clock BEFORE/AFTER measurement, mark it clearly as **unmeasured / complexity-only** and do not quote a timing or percentage speedup. Structural improvements such as bounded concurrency, fewer allocations, fewer SQL round-trips, or bounded retained metadata may be documented with those exact structural metrics.
- Benchmark-only PRs/MRs must write their measured output back into the canonical document before merge. CI logs are transient evidence, not the durable performance record. If the benchmark result is produced by CI, amend the documentation with that exact result and rerun the authoritative validation because the source tree changed.
- Keep accepted and rejected experiments in the performance document. A rejected index, cache, batching policy, or concurrency change should retain its measured data and rejection reason so the same low-value experiment is not repeated later.
- Large-scale scenarios must use stable, named workloads. When a subsystem claims 10k/100k scalability, document the exact logical item count, viewport/range behavior, thumbnail/cache state where relevant, and whether the run measures pure controller CPU, browser/Electron rendering, network/IPC transport, decode/generation, or end-to-end latency.
- Performance CI jobs should be scoped to the branch/workload that needs them unless they are stable enough to become a permanent regression gate. Do not turn a noisy exploratory benchmark into a required global CI gate before its variance and budget are understood.
- **Viewport/request-scoped cancellation performance:** when a virtual range, thumbnail or preview is no longer consumed after scrolling, navigation, view/window teardown, or lifecycle changes, propagate cancellation through the owning Web `AbortSignal` or Desktop Renderer → Main → Agent IPC down to the HTTP request context and Go handler; measure actual upstream abort, active request count and payload waste, not only stale-result suppression. Scoped cancellation must not terminate durable Task Center uploads, downloads, synchronization, deletion, or shared background maintenance merely because a window changes. Reused/background tasks need their own lifecycle and consumer-aware semantics.

- **Mandatory cross-platform performance acceptance (2026-10-12):** treat **native Desktop Electron**, **wide Web browser**, **Mobile Web browser**, **desktop installed PWA**, **Android installed PWA**, and **iOS installed PWA** as distinct workload dimensions; read the [cross-platform matrix](docs/performance-platform-coverage.md) together with the [deduplicated workload registry](docs/performance-test-registry.md) before assigning a new performance ID. For Gallery and FileExplorer, cover cold/warm 100k physical JPEG/H264/Live still/Live motion/RAW/HEVC/LIVP as applicable, real shared Grid/Details/Timeline virtual-scroll windows, decoded pixels/posters, bounded DOM/CPU/RSS/network and cancellation all the way to actual Go `Request.Context().Done`; distinct source codecs and real bytes must be reported. For 1/4 GiB transfers and 100k synchronize/delete, test real CAS integrity, progress, task-owned cancellation, pause/restart/resume and owner permissions by platform, including lossy/slow networks; keep view/window unload distinct from durable Server task ownership. Keep every untested device/mode **Not measured**, and record separate exact-source n≥3 CPU/RSS/latency/bytes evidence per platform (and actual installed-device observations when available); never infer iOS background execution from Web/SW/desktop CI or pretend physical iOS/Android measurements were performed. All completed new tests must update the existing central registry, platform matrix, relevant subsystem document and stable raw evidence together in the same one-work-commit PR; no repeated accepted workloads merely to fill a grid.

## Sidebar account quota versus storage-host capacity (2026-10-12)

- The persistent Web/Desktop Sidebar footer must be explicitly labeled **我的云端存储** and must remain **current-account** even while an administrator visits global pages. `physical_used_bytes` from `/me/quota` is owner-scoped deduplicated `storage_key` accounting, **not** independently attributable physical bytes on the host filesystem. For positive `quota_bytes`, only current-account used/quota/percent belongs to the primary progress bar.
- For unlimited account quota (`quota_bytes=0`), retain the user-requested server storage disk available space and optionally an explicitly named **服务器存储磁盘（非个人配额）** percent when both trustworthy disk total/available are provided. Never subtract account charges from host filesystem occupancy to show fake personal-vs-other physical segments. Unknown disk denominator must not fabricate a percentage; full disk warning is not an account quota error. Preserve both apps' shared footer and 52px App Frame. See [`docs/sidebar-capacity-scope.md`](docs/sidebar-capacity-scope.md).

## Local-storage cache scope contract (2026-10-12)

- The user/device area “本地存储” is **client-scoped, not the logged-in account's cloud storage**. Web/Mobile Web browser `Cache Storage` cleanup affects every cache namespace for the current browser profile and xDrive Origin, potentially shared by accounts used there; `navigator.storage.estimate` is an origin aggregate, not a per-account or guaranteed reclaimable-byte metric. Desktop Electron HTTP `session.defaultSession` cache likewise is not per-account, and is separate from current-device Agent on-demand file cache and offline pinning.
- Every shared Local Storage page and destructive cache confirmation must disclose the current browser/client/Agent scope and any cross-account regeneration impact. Never claim the operation clears a Server account quota, all other browser origins/profiles, or globally stored CAS files. Existing Web Cache Storage, Electron `clearCache` and Agent `releaseCache`/CfAPI contracts stay untouched. See [`docs/local-storage-scope.md`](docs/local-storage-scope.md).

## Instance-wide system maintenance entry (2026-10-12)

- The only UI entry for host-level **服务端更新** is administrator **管理 → 系统维护** (Web app `admin-maintenance`, Desktop matching view); never embed it in personal Settings or the 11-service **系统依赖** editor. Reuse `XDriveSystemMaintenancePage` with the existing shared update controller/card/confirmation and the existing Web REST vs Desktop Agent IPC adapters. The Server `requireAdmin` and restricted host command boundary remain authoritative; the Desktop *client* updater stays device-local in Settings.
- Host updates are durable and cannot be canceled merely by a window close or App navigation. Preserve 52px App Frame, Web hash/deep-link and compact navigation, Desktop role-demotion guard, capability-unavailable feedback and unchanged Push/Pull/Task Center. See [`docs/system-maintenance.md`](docs/system-maintenance.md).

## Administrator Web/Desktop functional parity (2026-10-12)

- **Explicit product decision:** Desktop administrator navigation and functionality must equal Web, not a permitted platform exception. In the identical order: 用户管理, 全局后台任务, 审计日志, 全局存储, 系统依赖, 系统维护. No read-only placeholder for Web write operations.
- Cross-platform administrator views must be one shared MUI component per page, fed by Web's authenticated REST or Desktop's explicit authenticated Renderer → Main → Agent IPC → Go Client → Server admin API. Do not export tokens into Desktop Renderer, use a generic privileged URL/path proxy, or weaken Server `requireAdmin()`, self/last-admin invariants or audit. Old Agents show an unavailable explanation instead of a nonfunctional button.
- Complete and merge C1 user management, C2 virtualized audit, C3 full global storage, and **C4 personal/global background task UI parity**, including tests, before reporting finished Sidebar parity or resuming the performance-only mainline. Track progress and evidence in [`docs/sidebar-admin-parity.md`](docs/sidebar-admin-parity.md).

## Sidebar privilege partitions (2026-10-12)

- **Before “管理” = signed-in owner/device operations only; after “管理” = administrator-only instance/global operations.** The shared Web/Desktop MUI Sidebar and compact Mobile Web App switcher must preserve the same section ownership and relative order. User-owned files, Gallery, Push/Pull, personal tasks and cloud storage stay before the boundary; device-local caches, conflicts and diagnostics also stay before it and must disclose their local scope. “全局后台任务”, user management, audit, instance-wide storage and system dependencies belong only to the role-gated “管理” section, never to the core destination list or a bottom extension after management. This is **navigation presentation**, not an authorization substitute: protect global endpoints with Server admin checks and preserve owning-device authorization separately.
- Preserve existing workspace route keys, 52px App Frame header, task navigation/deep links, user-only tasks and Desktop device-only diagnostics; do not collapse global maintenance into a personal task or infer that a Desktop device operation is instance-global. Tests must verify Web/Desktop full Sidebar and compact Mobile menus for ordinary/admin role and the admin-boundary ordering.

- The administrator destination is displayed as **全局后台任务**, explicitly meaning Server-side tasks across users and system maintenance; ordinary **任务** remains current-owner/local-scoped. Reuse the stable `global-tasks` workspace key, `tasks?scope=global` deep links, `requireAdmin` and Server `control_actions`. Do not conflate the list with transient Web/Desktop network transfer popovers.
- **C4 Task Center UI parity:** personal and global Server background tasks default to one shared MUI task card (status, progress, elapsed time, actions); global additionally shows actual owner/system/instance context and can optionally use a dense table on wide viewports, but mobile always uses cards. Personal FileOperation undo/redo/conflict actions and local transfers do not belong to global Server tasks. Do not change task ownership, `control_actions`, pagination or durable-task cancellation when unifying UI. See [`docs/transfers-and-tasks.md`](docs/transfers-and-tasks.md).

## UI policy

- **Gallery Mobile Web / wide Web feature-parity is mandatory (2026-10-10).** Follow `docs/mobile-gallery-ios27.md`. iOS 27 Photos is the high-fidelity mobile-only **presentation and interaction** reference; Mobile Web MUST expose every Gallery operation that wide Web exposes (directly, by Collections, More, selection toolbar, Search or inspector), preserving permissions, selection scope, errors, task receipts, album semantics, media/Live/RAW/Viewer operations and return identity. Both layouts use ONE Web `XDriveMediaGalleryPage`, ONE Web REST `MediaGalleryDataSource`, shared `VirtualCollection`/VirtualGrid/VirtualTimeline, common selection/query/edit/Properties/Viewer and Server Range contracts. No separate mobile Gallery endpoint, media index, dense item collection, business controller or alternative Viewer. Responsive preference defaults may differ only as presentation settings; Server search/filter/sort capabilities and logical results must be equivalent. Verify mobile/wide crossover at 899/900px, 10k/100k range behavior and end-to-end task results; never count static source checks as physical iOS acceptance. Keep the full-viewport Mobile App Frame and 52px header unchanged.

- **Gallery Places map provider (2026-10-10, normative):** Web/Desktop/Mobile Web render maps **only through Baidu Maps Server API** via the authenticated xDrive Server; AK never enters renderer code or browser URLs. The original offline SVG world/graticule map and any alternate/self-hosted/offline map fallback are **not supported**. When the provider is disabled, AK is missing, HTTP fails, or an old Agent/Server is in use, keep the map region visible with a clear unavailable/configuration message, not another map. GPS facets/location list and optional GeoNames place-label metadata are separate from map rendering and remain available. See `docs/baidu-map-server-api.md`; update tests if this contract changes.
- **Baidu Server AK admin configuration (2026-10-10, normative):** The administrator **系统依赖** page may edit, disable, clear and **explicitly reveal** only the Baidu Server AK. Reuse the Yike Cookie temporary reveal UI: masked by default, deliberate click, audited server-side reveal, a no-store privileged response, and automatic hiding after 30 seconds or on view/account change. Normal status/config APIs never include plaintext. Encrypt and persist the AK using xDrive's versioned server-side credential keyring; no plaintext database row, logs, audit metadata or status JSON. Enforce Server-side admin authorization, revision conflicts, and explicit clear confirmation. New map requests must use the latest persisted effective configuration **without restarting Server, Docker, uploads, downloads or sync**. Only missing bootstrap encryption keys may require a one-time deployment restart. Saved disabled/cleared configuration must not fall back to an old environment AK; unavailable Baidu must never fall back to another map.

- **Mobile follow-up scope is normative.** Follow the user-approved order in `docs/mobile-web-followups.md`; do not turn unselected iOS comparison suggestions into implementation work. Below 900 CSS px, FileExplorer exposes only its current browsing context with **no tab bar or hidden internal tab commands**, including with attached mouse/keyboard. Preserve the same mounted workspace/history and desktop tab state for wide return. Record actual 44px location/filter hit targets, focus/lifecycle behavior and renderer evidence separately from the physical iOS/Android browser/installed-mode, keyboard, safe-area and VoiceOver matrix.

- **Mobile Web App Frame and full-screen layout are normative (2026-10-09).** Read `docs/mobile-web.md` and `docs/web-app-runtime.md` before changing Web App navigation, FileExplorer, Gallery, or Viewer. Below 900 CSS px, the **App Frame**, not the inner scrolling `main`, fills the entire dynamic viewport (x=0, y=0, full width/height). Its own 52px title bar (plus genuine top safe area) owns an explicit left **exit current App** action and top-right app-switch and upload/download actions; inner `main` receives the remaining height and retains its mounted scroll owner. No global floating navigation trigger, permanent global AppBar/footer/sidebar, reserved global spacer or desktop outer padding may cover App content/status. App switching is a Drawer reached from the App title bar; account/settings stay reachable inside it. Workspace App exit restores the previous App history entry, NOT the FileExplorer parent directory; a direct deep-link without a caller falls back to Overview. Viewer uses its existing full-viewport overlay header and own return semantics; never remount its caller. Mobile short tap opens, stationary hold shows context menu, and held move drags only when a valid destination/operation exists. Explicit Select and keyboard/menu alternatives remain; mobile file/photo tiles must not overlay Favorite/Info/More action buttons, but compact noninteractive Live/video/sync/duplicate badges are allowed. Preserve native scroll/pinch, Live Photo hold-to-play, text selection, Desktop controls, and browser Back/Forward. Validate actual Frame/header/main/status geometry, safe areas, long hold vs scroll/drag cancellation, 899/900px, 10k/100k virtualization, and iOS/Android device results separately from simulation.
- **Web/Mobile Web Files functional equivalence (2026-10-10):** Every wide-Web FileExplorer business capability is required on Mobile Web: operation permissions and validation, create/upload/download/copy/cut/paste/rename/move/delete, undo/redo, clipboard and path-copy, Search/filters/sort/grouping, folder Properties/statistics/provenance, thumbnails/media, favorites/recent/quick access, tags/saved searches, trash, share, history/navigation, errors/retries and cancellation. **Only internal multi-tab UI and its commands** may be omitted on Mobile due to screen size; replace any other dense desktop affordance with a reachable touch/keyboard/menu alternative. Both layouts must use the same Web REST adapters and stateful business controllers, **shared virtual collection** with Server-authoritative paged ranges, grouping and sparse-window cancellation, and shared `ui/shared` MUI business/thumbnail/Properties components. Mobile may independently render iOS Files chrome and layouts but must not fork transport, authorization, list pagination semantics, or business actions. Record a paired wide/375px/390px/899px/900px functional/permission/error regression matrix, 10k/100k bounded-list evidence and physical iOS/Android results separately. Treat any unverified or missing capability as a gap, not as parity.
- **iOS 27 Files 1:1 reference contract (2026-10-10):** `docs/mobile-files-ios27.md` is the explicit and version-locked visual/interaction acceptance baseline for Mobile Web Files, **not merely an iOS-inspired style guide**. Match Apple's iOS 27 Files behavior and layouts for corresponding real features, with screenshot-diff and interaction-state evidence before claiming 1:1. Preserve xDrive's full-dynamic-viewport App Frame and its separate **52px global App Header**, upload/download action and App switching, Web/Desktop shared Server/API and one shared workspace/virtual-collection/windowing/thumbnail/Properties contract. Only internal multi-file tabs may be omitted from Mobile Web; all other available wide-Web file functions require reachable mobile controls. Never fabricate a Shared-to-me view, folder-scoped Search, system document scanner, folder colors or iOS byte-perfect assets without the underlying functionality or measured licensed reference. Where Apple's current tab model or native capabilities differ from existing xDrive functionality, record the precise open gap rather than falsely claiming native parity. The new iOS 27 benchmark supersedes vague "iOS style" descriptions, but does not remove the user-approved functionality, security or existing App Frame.
- **Mobile Web Files iOS presentation (Q1–Q6, 2026-10-09):** Read `docs/mobile-files-ios.md` before modifying Files. Below 900 CSS px Web Files renders a dedicated Mobile Files component, not the reduced Desktop `XDriveFileExplorer` surface. Keep the internal Files-only Recent/Browse/Favorites rail, per-account Browse-home/last-folder+scroll contract, collapsible all-files Search, top-right More command menu and blue-folder/two-line List/Grid. Reuse existing Web REST/workspace/controllers and Viewer; do not add Mobile-only API, fake folder-scoped Search, global floating/bottom navigation or per-item overlay buttons. Native iOS/Android tests remain distinct from Chromium. Q1–Q4 App Frame rules above remain unchanged.
- Use **MUI (Material UI)** for all newly implemented Web and Desktop renderer UI. Prefer MUI layout, form, feedback, dialog, navigation, and display components over introducing new Ant Design or bespoke HTML/CSS component patterns.
- Existing Ant Design and bespoke Desktop UI does **not** need a one-shot migration. When a task materially touches an existing UI surface, opportunistically migrate the touched controls/components to MUI when doing so is low-risk and keeps the PR focused.
- `ui/shared` has two explicit layers: framework-neutral shared models/view-models/formatting/state derivation under `ui/shared/src`, and the canonical shared React/MUI component layer under `ui/shared/src/mui`.
- When Web and Desktop present the same business concept, first reuse or extend `@xdrive/ui/mui` instead of creating parallel app-local MUI implementations. Shared dialogs, forms, page/workspace composition, status/metric presentation, navigation chrome, Source UI, FileExplorer UI, Gallery UI, Task Center UI, and similar cross-client surfaces belong in the shared MUI layer when their interaction contract is materially the same.
- Keep platform adapters local. Web REST calls, Desktop Agent IPC, Electron/native-window chrome, OS integration, Desktop-only sync/cache/client-update behavior should stay in their owning app and feed shared components through typed props/adapters rather than being moved into shared rendering code.
- Do not duplicate cross-surface Source/status/formatting rules or common business presentation in Web and Desktop. Put framework-neutral semantics in `ui/shared/src`, common React/MUI rendering in `ui/shared/src/mui`, and only platform-specific orchestration in each app.
- When waiting on GitHub/GitLab CI for the current PR, use that time to **plan** the next small feature: inspect the relevant interfaces, tests, dependency chain, and branch strategy. Do not modify or open the next feature branch until the current small feature is merged, unless the work is an explicitly approved stacked dependency.
